text:
****#Clemson vs #CharlestonASouthern preview & prediction *****

CLEMSON, S.C. — When the Clemson Tigers return to Death Valley on Saturday afternoon to take on the Charleston Southern Buccaneers, there will be more at stake than simply adding another victory to the win column.

For Dabo Swinney and his Clemson football program, Saturday represents an opportunity to correct mistakes, develop younger players, establish consistency along both lines of scrimmage, and showcase the depth that could become critically important during the second half of the 2026 season.

Clemson enters the contest at 3-2 following its bye week and a disappointing 41-13 loss to Miami. Charleston Southern arrives at 3-3, fresh off an impressive 49-39 victory over South Carolina State.

The Tigers will undoubtedly be the more talented team on paper, but the Buccaneers aren’t coming to Clemson simply to collect a paycheck. Charleston Southern has some momentum, and its special teams have demonstrated an ability to change games.

Game Information

Matchup: Clemson Tigers vs. Charleston Southern Buccaneers
Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026
Kickoff: Noon ET
Television: ACC Network
Location: Memorial Stadium, Clemson, South Carolina
Clemson Sports News Prediction: Clemson 45, Charleston Southern 13
Clemson’s Offense vs. Charleston Southern’s Defense
Quarterbacks: An Opportunity for Tait Reynolds to Take Another Step
The development of freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds remains one of the biggest storylines surrounding this Clemson football team.

Reynolds has shown flashes of the talent that made him such an intriguing prospect. Against Miami, he threw for a career-high 295 yards, including several impressive connections with Bryant Wesco Jr., who finished with nine receptions for 152 yards.

Those are encouraging numbers against a talented opponent, but the challenge now is turning those flashes into consistent production.

Against Charleston Southern, Reynolds should have opportunities to work through his progressions, develop timing with his receivers, and gain a better understanding of what Clemson wants to accomplish offensively.

The Tigers need more than impressive individual throws. They need sustained drives, third-down conversions, and touchdowns in the red zone.

If Clemson builds a comfortable lead, Saturday could also provide valuable playing time for Christopher Vizzina, Brock Bradley, or other available reserve quarterbacks.

Advantage: Clemson

Running Backs: Establishing the Ground Game
If there is one area where Clemson should be able to dictate Saturday’s contest, it is on the ground.

Gideon Davidson continues to develop into a central part of Clemson’s offensive identity. His combination of quickness, vision, and physical running style gives the Tigers a weapon capable of controlling the tempo.

Chris Johnson Jr., David Eziomume, and Jay Haynes provide additional options in the backfield.

But the biggest question isn’t necessarily about the running backs themselves. It’s about the offensive line.

Clemson has struggled at times to establish consistent movement along the line of scrimmage, particularly with the changes and uncertainty on the right side.

Against Charleston Southern, those issues cannot continue.

The Buccaneers have allowed approximately 127 rushing yards per game through their first six contests. Clemson should be able to exceed that number, particularly if the offensive line consistently wins its individual battles.

This should be a game where the Tigers establish the run early and create manageable second- and third-down situations.

Advantage: Clemson

Wide Receivers: Time to Showcase the Young Talent
Clemson’s receiving corps may be one of the more intriguing groups to watch Saturday.

Bryant Wesco Jr. is coming off an excellent performance against Miami, and the connection developing between Wesco and Reynolds has the potential to become one of Clemson’s biggest offensive strengths.

T.J. Moore, Tyler Brown, and the remainder of Clemson’s experienced receivers should find opportunities against the Buccaneers.

But this is also where Clemson needs to begin showcasing its younger talent.

Freshman Gordon Sellars III is a player we would love to see receive meaningful offensive snaps. At 6-foot-3, he brings size and potential to the outside receiving positions.

Naeem Burroughs is another exciting young player who deserves opportunities with the football in his hands.

Burroughs brings speed and playmaking potential that Clemson could utilize through quick passes, crossing routes, screens, and other opportunities to create space.

Saturday would be an excellent occasion to see how those younger receivers respond when given opportunities in live game situations.

Charleston Southern has surrendered nearly 195 passing yards per game but has also produced five interceptions. Clemson cannot become careless with the football.

Advantage: Clemson

Tight Ends: Developing Another Offensive Weapon
The tight end position provides another opportunity for Clemson to experiment and develop depth.

Olsen Patt-Henry and Christian Bentancur provide experience, but the Tigers should look to expand opportunities for freshman Tayveon Wilson.

Wilson is exactly the type of young player who could benefit from extended second-half action.

Getting him involved in the passing game while allowing him to experience meaningful blocking assignments would provide valuable repetitions that simply cannot be duplicated on the practice field.

The Tigers should challenge their tight ends to become more productive targets, particularly in the red zone.

Advantage: Clemson

Offensive Line: Perhaps Clemson’s Most Important Position Group
Forget the final score for a moment.

If there is one offensive position group that Clemson Sports News will be watching closely, it’s the offensive line.

Clemson has been searching for consistency, especially on the right side. Injuries, personnel changes, and the search for the right combination have contributed to an offense that has struggled to find a reliable rhythm.

Saturday offers a chance to evaluate combinations and develop younger players.

Freshman Chance Barclay is one of the players we would particularly like to see get into the game. The same goes for other younger linemen who could eventually be called upon during the demanding ACC schedule ahead.

These players need more than a handful of meaningless snaps at the end of a blowout. They need actual possessions where they can work through assignments, communicate protections, and establish chemistry.

Clemson’s offensive line should be physically superior to Charleston Southern’s defensive front.

The question is whether that superiority will translate into the consistent execution that has been missing at times this season.

Advantage: Clemson — but the performance must match the talent.

Charleston Southern’s Offense vs. Clemson’s Defense
Charleston Southern’s offense presents an interesting challenge because the Buccaneers are coming off one of their best performances of the season.

Under head coach Gabe Giardina, Charleston Southern has averaged approximately 27.8 points and 281 total yards per game.

The Buccaneers have averaged 136.3 rushing yards and 144.5 passing yards per contest through six games.

Those aren’t overwhelming numbers, but Clemson’s defense cannot afford to overlook an opponent coming off a confidence-building victory.

Defensive Line: Clemson Must Reestablish Control Up Front
This is an area where Clemson needs to demonstrate noticeable improvement.

The Tigers have dealt with injuries and personnel changes along the interior defensive line, and the results have occasionally been troubling.

There have been stretches when opposing offenses have found too much room between the tackles. At other times, Clemson has struggled to maintain gap discipline and finish tackles near the line of scrimmage.

Against Charleston Southern, the Tigers need to reestablish their presence up front.

The Buccaneers have a capable rushing attack led by Hakeem Watters, who rushed for 72 yards against South Carolina State and added a 24-yard touchdown.

Charleston Southern will attempt to establish the run, keep the game manageable, and prevent Clemson from turning its defensive front loose in obvious passing situations.

Clemson should be able to win this matchup, but execution will matter.

This is also an ideal opportunity to develop younger defensive linemen such as Kourtney Kelly and Kam Cody, along with other available reserves.

Getting those players meaningful snaps could prove valuable as Clemson prepares for the remaining ACC schedule.

Advantage: Clemson

Linebackers: Sammy Brown Continues to Lead the Way
Sammy Brown has been one of the most consistent performers on Clemson’s defense this season.

His athleticism, physicality, and ability to pursue plays from sideline to sideline make him a critical part of the Tigers’ defensive identity.

Brown and the linebacking corps should have opportunities to make plays against Charleston Southern.

However, they will need to remain disciplined.

The Buccaneers use their running backs and quarterbacks to create different looks, and Clemson cannot afford to become overly aggressive and allow cutback lanes or missed assignments.

The objective should be straightforward: win on first down, limit explosive runs, and force Charleston Southern into passing situations.

If Clemson accomplishes those three things, the Buccaneers will have difficulty sustaining drives.

Advantage: Clemson

Secondary: Ashton Hampton and Clemson’s Defensive Backfield Should Shine
This might be Clemson’s strongest defensive matchup of the afternoon.

Ashton Hampton has been outstanding in the Tigers’ secondary, and his play continues to strengthen his reputation as one of the premier cornerbacks in college football.

Hampton’s combination of size, athleticism, coverage skills, and physicality makes him an incredibly difficult assignment for opposing receivers.

Charleston Southern has experienced a recent change at quarterback.

Jared Echols made his first career start against South Carolina State and responded with 194 passing yards and three touchdowns, completing 17 of 29 attempts. He also added 28 rushing yards.

Wide receiver Mekhi Campfield caught five passes for 82 yards and two touchdowns in that victory.

Those numbers suggest Charleston Southern has enough playmaking ability to challenge Clemson if the Tigers become careless.

But the Buccaneers will be facing a significant increase in defensive talent.

Clemson’s secondary should be able to challenge receivers at the line of scrimmage, disrupt passing lanes, and create opportunities for turnovers.

Advantage: Clemson

Donovan Starr: An Important Opportunity for Defensive Development
One of the most important personnel developments heading into Saturday involves Clemson’s secondary.

With the Tigers dealing with a season-ending injury in their defensive backfield, Clemson must establish a dependable rotation and develop younger players who may be called upon to assume greater responsibilities.

Donovan Starr is one of those players.

Starr needs repetitions.

He needs experience communicating with the safeties, recognizing offensive formations, and adjusting to the responsibilities that come with increased playing time.

Clemson needs to discover which combinations work best before the competition becomes significantly more demanding.

The Tigers have the defensive backfield talent to remain one of the better coverage units in the conference. However, replacing injured contributors requires preparation, chemistry, and experience.

Saturday provides an ideal opportunity to work toward all three.

Advantage: Clemson

Special Teams: The Buccaneers Have Some Dangerous Weapons
This might be the most interesting matchup of the entire contest.

Clemson’s special teams have been one of the bright spots of the 2026 season.

The Tigers have produced a punt-return touchdown, enjoyed reliable field-goal production, and generally performed well in the kicking game.

But Charleston Southern deserves considerable respect in this department.

In its victory over South Carolina State, the Buccaneers scored two special-teams touchdowns.

Hakeem Watters returned a punt 60 yards for a touchdown, while Quay Kindell added a spectacular 98-yard kickoff return.

That is no small accomplishment.

Charleston Southern has also demonstrated reliability in its kicking game, converting its first four field-goal attempts through six contests.

The Buccaneers have averaged approximately 30.3 yards per kickoff return and 12.9 yards per punt return.

Those numbers should get Clemson’s attention.

The Tigers cannot allow Charleston Southern to manufacture points through the return game.

Clemson’s coverage units must maintain lane discipline, tackle effectively, and avoid giving the Buccaneers opportunities to flip field position.

Advantage: Clemson overall — but Charleston Southern’s return game is a legitimate threat.

Position-by-Position Matchup Breakdown
Position GroupAdvantage
QuarterbacksClemson
Running BacksClemson
Wide ReceiversClemson
Tight EndsClemson
Offensive LineClemson
Defensive LineClemson
LinebackersClemson
SecondaryClemson
Kicking GameClemson
Return GameCompetitive
Overall DepthClemson
The difference in overall roster talent and depth strongly favors the Tigers. However, games aren’t played on recruiting rankings, and Clemson must approach this contest with the same attention to detail it would bring to an ACC opponent.

The Biggest Objective: Building Depth for the Second Half of the Season
This is where Saturday’s contest becomes much more interesting than the final score.

Clemson has a demanding stretch ahead, and the Tigers will almost certainly need contributions from players who have not yet received significant playing time.

The coaching staff should approach this matchup with that reality in mind.

Gordon Sellars III — Wide Receiver: Give the freshman opportunities to work against live coverage, particularly on the outside. His size provides Clemson with another potential weapon in the passing game.

Naeem Burroughs — Wide Receiver: Find creative ways to get him the football. His development could add another explosive element to an offense searching for consistency.

Chance Barclay — Offensive Line: Give him an opportunity to experience meaningful snaps. Clemson needs to develop quality depth along the offensive line, especially with continuing questions on the right side.

Tayveon Wilson — Tight End: Get the freshman involved in the offense. Let him experience blocking responsibilities and give him opportunities as a receiver.

Donovan Starr — Defensive Back: Perhaps one of the most important players to evaluate. With Clemson needing to replace contributions lost to injury, Starr can use this game to become more comfortable in the defensive rotation.

The same applies to Clemson’s younger defensive linemen and reserve linebackers.

There is absolutely nothing wrong with allowing your starters to establish control of a football game.

But once that control has been established, Saturday should become an opportunity to develop the next wave of Clemson football players.

The Tigers cannot afford to reach November and discover they lack experienced replacements when injuries or fatigue begin taking their toll.

That preparation needs to begin now.

Five Keys to a Clemson Victory
1. Start Fast and Take Control Early

Clemson cannot afford another sluggish offensive opening. Establish the run, get Reynolds comfortable, and force Charleston Southern to play from behind.

2. Dominate the Line of Scrimmage

This is particularly important on the offensive right side and along Clemson’s interior defensive line. Winning the physical battles should be nonnegotiable.

3. Eliminate Special-Teams Mistakes

Charleston Southern’s explosive return game is capable of creating momentum-changing plays. Clemson must avoid allowing the Buccaneers to steal possessions or easy points.

4. Get the Young Players Meaningful Experience

Sellars, Burroughs, Wilson, Barclay, Starr, and the younger defensive linemen should all be part of the developmental plan where health and game circumstances permit.

5. Finish Drives With Touchdowns

Clemson has struggled with red-zone efficiency this season. Settling for field goals against Charleston Southern would represent another missed opportunity to improve an area that must get better.

Clemson Sports News Prediction: Clemson 45, Charleston Southern 13
Charleston Southern deserves credit for its recent victory over South Carolina State and for the confidence it will bring into Death Valley.

But Clemson simply has too much talent, size, speed, and depth across the roster.

We expect the Tigers to establish control early, with Reynolds finding success in the passing game and Davidson helping create balance on the ground.

Clemson’s defense should limit Charleston Southern’s offensive opportunities, although the Buccaneers have enough playmaking ability to generate some points, especially if they can manufacture a short field or create an explosive special-teams play.

Look for Clemson to build a comfortable halftime advantage before beginning to work additional players into the lineup during the second half.

This shouldn’t be a game where the Tigers need to leave their starters on the field deep into the fourth quarter.

And frankly, we’d be disappointed if that were necessary.

Final Thoughts: This Game Is About the Future as Much as the Present
Clemson fans have every right to be disappointed with certain aspects of the Tigers’ performance through the first five games.

The offensive line has struggled with consistency. The defense has occasionally been vulnerable against the run. And the offense continues to search for sustained productivity.

But there have also been encouraging developments.

Reynolds is growing into his role at quarterback. Wesco is demonstrating his potential to become an elite playmaker. Hampton continues to shine in the defensive backfield. Sammy Brown has been a consistent presence at linebacker, and Clemson’s special teams have provided reasons for optimism.

Saturday is an opportunity to build on those positives.

More importantly, it is an opportunity for Dabo Swinney and his staff to begin preparing the next group of contributors for the challenges ahead.

The Tigers still have Virginia Tech, Florida State, Syracuse, Georgia Tech, Duke, and South Carolina remaining on the schedule.

That is a demanding stretch of football.

Clemson needs healthy starters, improved execution, and young players who are prepared to contribute when called upon.

So yes, Clemson should beat Charleston Southern, and beat them convincingly. But the real measure of success Saturday won’t simply be the points on the scoreboard.

It will be whether the Tigers leave Death Valley a better, deeper, more confident football team than they were when they entered it.

That’s what Clemson needs coming out of the bye week.

And that’s what we’ll be watching.

FINAL PREDICTION: CLEMSON 45, CHARLESTON SOUTHERN 13

Dear Elon, @elonmusk 
I hope this finds you well, ideally somewhere between a product demo and a productive night on X.

URGENT NATIONAL PRESS RELEASE
FLORIDA MUST ACT NOW — GOVERNOR DESANTIS: TAKE ADVANTAGE OF THIS OFFER IMMEDIATELY AHEAD OF THE MIDTERMS
Edina, Minnesota — October 15, 2026
Thomas Evenstad of Edina, Minnesota, today issues an urgent call to action to Governor Ron DeSantis and the State of Florida:
TAKE ADVANTAGE OF THIS OFFER REACH OUT TO ME!!!
With the midterms rapidly approaching, FL has a narrow window to lead the nation once again. I stand ready to consult immediately on the landmark VIOLENT DANGEROUS PREDATORS ACT (VDP ACT) — the first-in-the-nation expansion of Florida’s proven Jimmy Ryce Act — for a one-time fee of only $5,000 plus travel and meals.
TIME IS CRITICAL
The midterms are the moment to show Florida voters — and the entire country — decisive leadership on violent crime. Delaying means missing the chance to campaign on a concrete, groundbreaking solution that will permanently remove more than 60 percent of the most active violent criminals from Florida streets.

THE PROVEN FOUNDATION: FLORIDA’S JIMMY RYCE ACT
Florida already set the national standard with the Jimmy Ryce Involuntary Civil Commitment for Sexually Violent Predators’ Treatment and Care Act (Florida Statutes Chapter 394). Passed in 1998 after the tragic 1995 kidnapping, rape, and murder of nine-year-old Jimmy Ryce, the law allows the State to civilly commit — after criminal sentences are completed — individuals who:
Have been convicted of a sexually violent offense, and
Suffer from a mental abnormality or personality disorder making them likely to reoffend sexually if not confined for long-term control, care, and treatment.
This civil process has kept the most dangerous sexual predators locked away and treated, protecting Florida’s children and families. PROTECTION TO ALL VIOLENT PREDATORS
The VDP ACT builds directly on this successful model and extends the same protective framework to a broader class of violent dangerous predators — chronic, high-rate offenders with repeated convictions for serious violent crimes who demonstrate a mental abnormality or personality disorder that makes them highly likely to reoffend violently if released.
Core elements of the VDP ACT:
Mandatory multi-agency screening of high-risk violent offenders before release
Full due-process civil commitment proceedings requiring clear and convincing evidence
Secure facilities dedicated to long-term management of those adjudicated as violent dangerous predators
COST-BENEFIT IMPACT: TRANSFORMING EVERY PART OF FLORIDA SOCIETY
By systematically identifying and civilly committing this small but extremely dangerous cohort, Florida can realistically remove more than 60 percent of the most active violent criminals from circulation.
Immediate and lasting benefits across society:
Law Enforcement: Fewer assaults on officers, reduced emergency calls, lower overtime and investigation costs
Judicial System & District Attorneys: Dramatically lighter caseloads and reduced court backlog
Hospitals & Trauma Centers: Sharp decline in gunshot, stabbing, and assault admissions — freeing capacity and cutting uncompensated care costs
Taxpayers & Communities: Safer neighborhoods, stronger economic growth, and restored quality of life
The human cost of inaction cannot be quantified. Every life saved and every family spared the trauma of violent crime is priceless. Over a ten-year period, the fiscal savings to Florida are projected in the billions to trillions of dollars when accounting for avoided incarceration, medical care, lost productivity, and the long-term societal costs of recidivism.
CALL TO ACTION — REACH OUT NOW
Governor DeSantis and Florida leadership:
Take advantage of this offer immediately.
Contact Thomas Evenstad of Edina, Minnesota, today.
For a one-time consulting fee of $5,000 plus travel and meals, I will work directly with your office and legislative leaders to draft, refine, and position the VDP ACT so Florida can lead the nation and deliver real results for voters this midterm season.

text:
•VA opened 43 new healthcare clinics, expanding access for Veterans around the country.
•The backlog of Veterans waiting for VA benefits is down more than 70% since Jan. 20, 2025, after it increased 24% during the Biden Administration. In June, this backlog fell to less than 70,000 claims for the first time since 2020.
•As of October, VA has enrolled more than 290,000 new Veterans in VA healthcare in 2026.
•Since Jan. 20, 2025, VA has offered Veterans more than 3.4 million appointments outside of normal operating hours. These early-morning, evening, and weekend appointments are giving Veterans more timely and convenient options for care.
•VA put the deployment of VA’s electronic health modernization effort back on track by successfully deploying it to four sites in Ohio and Kentucky, four sites in Michigan, and three sites in Indiana after the Biden Administration ignored this priority for years.
•VA will spend nearly $5 billion in FY26 to modernize, repair and improve healthcare facilities, the largest non-recurring maintenance investment in VA’s history.
•VA’s average disability claims processing time is down 46% since Jan. 20, 2025.
•VA completed a record high 82,083,918 direct care appointments in FY 2025, up 4.1% from FY 2024.
•VA completed a record high 59,989,662 community care appointments in FY 2025, up 12% from FY 2024.
•VA permanently housed 51,936 homeless Veterans across the country in FY25, the highest total in seven years.
•VA strengthened informed consent transparency for Veterans who are prescribed with psychotropic medications.
•VA processed 3 million disability compensation payments in FY2026 in record time, for the second straight year.
•VA announced an insurance premium holiday that will save Veterans nearly $150 million in life insurance payments.
•VA awarded a record high $1.17 billion in grants to fight Veteran homelessness.
•VA has eliminated the backlog of Veteran families waiting for VA healthcare.
•VA launched a new program to help homeless Veterans with $29 million worth of emergency supplies and transportation services.
•VA secured more than $10 billion in pharmaceutical price reductionsin FY2026, a record high that will enable VA to treat more Veterans.
•VA launched a psilocybin trial for Veterans with treatment-resistant depression.
•VA reduced paperwork by nearly two thirds for Veterans and survivors applying for VA benefits.
•VA launched a trial of GLP-1 treatment for alcohol use disorder that will take place in 18 VA facilities across the country.
•VA signed an agreement with the Department of Health and Human Services to improve cooperation on psychedelic drug trials that could help Veterans with serious mental illness.
•VA centralized its payroll for all VA employees instead of letting dozens of VA facilities run their own wasteful and duplicative payroll systems, a change that will save $24 million per year and allow VA to focus more resources on Veterans instead of bureaucracy.
•VA made long-overdue fixes to its police force, which will create a more stable VA Police and boost safety for Veterans, staff and visitors at VA locations across the country.
•VA launched a new Partial Claims Program that will help Veterans avoid foreclosure.
•VA sped up the delivery of prosthetic limbs to Veterans and is expecting a 42% reduction in delivery times.
•VA set new records for Veteran suicide prevention screening and comprehensive evaluations for at-risk Veterans, two critical elements of VA’s ongoing work to prevent Veteran suicide.
•78% of VA hospitals that received an Overall Hospital Quality Star Rating earned four or five stars in the latest annual report from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services – a record high.
•VA launched a clinical trial of MDMA-assisted mental health therapy to assess how it may be used to treat severe mental health disorders, including posttraumatic stress disorder & alcohol use

BARC developed & IREL piloted rare earth & titanium technologies at RETTP, Bhopal. All 7 were recently offered for ToT to startups, MSMEs & entrepreneurs (AIC Anushakti):

La, Ce, Nd metal, NdPr recovery from NdFeB magnets
Lamp & LED phosphor (key Yttrium use case), and Ti sponge.

Nearly all address mid/downstream gaps where India remains heavily import-dependent. The timing dovetails with the Sintered REPM scheme, backing private oxide-to-magnet lines, further incentivising ToT.

Things are changing. AIC recently signed 22 ToT & 2 incubation agreements, but mostly in healthcare, energy & waste tech—not deep/critical tech.

BARC, CSIR, etc. have long offered crazy IP portfolios, yet few Indian players take the commercialisation risk. Precisely why Ashvini (AREPL) & Raana (RSPL) deserve credit.

RETTP's ToT progress by 2027 would be an important yardstick of domestic intent.

text:
Chief Minister lays foundation stone for Holistic Institute of Ayurveda and Wellness Centre at Lungchok

Pakyong, October 15 (IPR): Chief Minister, Mr Prem Singh Tamang, laid the foundation stone for the Holistic Institute of Ayurveda and Wellness Centre at Lungchok, Pakyong District, today.

The programme was organised by the Department of AYUSH, Government of Sikkim, marking a significant step towards strengthening AYUSH infrastructure and promoting holistic healthcare in the State.

The occassion was attended by Cabinet Ministers; MLAs; Advisors; Zilla Adhyaksha, Zilla Upadhyaksha, Pakyong District; Mayor; Chairman and Chairperson from various departments; Heads of Offices; Additional Political Secretary to the Chief Minister; Press Secretary to the Chief Minister; Former MLAs; District Collector, Pakyong; Superintendent of Police, Pakyong District; Confidential Assistant to the Chief Minister; Officers on Special Duty from various departments and SDM Rongli.

During the ceremony, Chief Minister, Mr Prem Singh Tamang, congratulated the people of Chujachen constituency on the establishment of the Holistic Institute of Ayurveda and Wellness Centre in the constituency. He also acknowledged the efforts of the organising department and various stakeholders in working towards the realisation of the project.

He noted that beyond strengthening traditional healthare, the project will promote welness tourism and emphasised the state government's commitment to preventive healthcare and public well being.

The Chief Minister highlighted various developmental initiatives undertaken by the State Government in the health, education and infrastructure sectors. Referring to proposed and ongoing works in the constituency, he emphasised the importance of road connectivity, maintenance and improvement in supporting local development and strengthening tourism.

He highlighted various welfare measures undertaken by the State Government for government employees, underprivileged sections of society, ASHA workers and Anganwadi workers. Referring to the Sikkim Aama Sashaktikaran Yojana, he noted the recent distribution of assistance under the scheme and shared that the Government intends to extend its coverage to more beneficiaries. He further spoke about initiatives aimed at supporting vulnerable families and improving their overall well-being.

Speaking on housing, the Chief Minister informed that allotments under the Sikkim Garib Awas Yojana would be handed over to beneficiaries soon, with priority given to cases requiring urgent assistance. He also indicated that the Government intends to extend the scheme to cover more beneficiaries.

In addition, the Chief Minister touched upon revenue and capital expenditure, emphasising the importance of effective financial management. He further stressed the importance of work culture, punctuality, time management and dedication to duty.

Referring to the concept of dignity of labour in Western countries, he called for the development of a system that recognises and respects all forms of work and for its integration into the existing work culture.

Highlighting the employment potential of the proposed wellness centre, the Chief Minister urged the concerned authorities to provide appropriate training for the engagement in the facility. He emphasised the importance of developing local human resources to support the centre’s operations.

The Chief Minister also informed that he would undertake three-day visits to each constituency under the Jan Bhetghat programme to interact with the public, listen to their concerns and understand their needs.

Further, the Chief Minister called upon the local community, officials and other stakeholders to work collectively towards developing the Holistic Institute of Ayurveda and Wellness Centre into a prominent wellness destination.

Earlier, the Chief Minister unveiled the project plaque and performed Bhumi Puja at the venue, seeking blessings for the successful construction and completion of the project.

In his address, Minister for Agriculture, Horticulture, AH&VS Department, and Fisheries Department cum MLA Chujachen, Mr Puran Kumar Gurung, expressed his appreciation to the State Government for selecting Chujachen constituency for the establishment of the institute.

He also highlighted various developmental initiatives undertaken by the State Government in the constituency, including improvements in public amenities, infrastructure and essential services. He briefly outlined ongoing and proposed development works, including road improvement, carpeting and bridge-related projects, while acknowledging the Government’s continued focus on local development.

The Minister further touched upon various State Government initiatives in tourism, financial assistance and welfare, including schemes aimed at supporting women. Emphasising the importance of collective efforts, he acknowledged the role of different stakeholders in the overall development of the district. He also encouraged the youth to make the most of the opportunities offered by the institute and explore its wider potential in the fields of wellness, traditional healthcare and related avenues.

Minister for Health and Family Welfare Department, AYUSH and Culture Department, Mr GT Dhungel emphasised the potential of Ayurveda and traditional systems of healing, noting that greater engagement of the younger generation in this field could open up diverse livelihood opportunities and contribute to the well-being of society. He highlighted the long-standing significance of traditional healing practices and their role in addressing various health concerns.

He spoke about the suitability of Lungchok for the proposed wellness centre, noting that its natural surroundings could provide a peaceful environment conducive to relaxation and well-being. He outlined the potential of the institute in promoting Ayurveda, traditional healthcare practices and holistic wellness, while underscoring the importance of integrating these systems with existing healthcare services.

During her address, Secretary, Department of AYUSH, Mrs Suchitra Rasaily, highlighted the Department’s efforts to strengthen and expand AYUSH services in the State. She acknowledged the support of the State Government in advancing various initiatives of the Department, which has been working towards improving its services and outreach since its establishment.

She described the proposed wellness centre as an important addition to Sikkim’s healthcare and wellness landscape, with the potential to contribute to holistic well-being, research, awareness and human resource development. She also highlighted its prospects for promoting wellness tourism and creating livelihood opportunities for local communities.

Emphasising the relevance of traditional knowledge alongside scientific approaches, she noted that the centre represented a forward-looking initiative aligned with the broader vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. She expressed confidence that the initiative would contribute to the State’s long-term goals in healthcare, tourism, livelihood generation and youth development.

Chief Engineer, Department of AYUSH and Health and Family Welfare Department, Mr Sanjay Singh, presented the technical report, outlining the proposed infrastructure and key components of the project. He informed that the project, spread across approximately 50 acres, would comprise two major components, a Wellness Centre and a Happiness Centre.

He briefed the gathering on the proposed facilities, including nature-based recreational spaces, walking trails, cottages and the restoration of water bodies, among other features. He also highlighted the locational advantages of the site and the project’s potential to position Sikkim on the wider wellness tourism map.

Highlighting the broader vision behind the initiative, he noted that the project aligned with the State Government’s vision of Sunaulo, Samriddha ani Samartha Sikkim, with a focus on mental well-being and holistic health. He emphasised the integration of nature, healthy food, yoga and wellness practices under a approach to promoting a healthy, happy and balanced lifestyle, with a shift in focus from illness to wellness and from wellness to happiness.

Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of Habuild Health Tech Pvt. Ltd., Mr Saurabh Bothra, emphasised the importance of consistency in yoga practice and demonstrated yoga exercises for the participants. He also led the gathering in taking the “Happy and Healthy” pledge.

Earlier, the Engineering Cell, Department of AYUSH briefed the delegates on the project, outlining its plan, design and key features.

During the ceremony, the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Department of AYUSH and Habuild Health Tech Pvt. Ltd. was witnessed.

The programme also witnessed the presentation of a Certificate of Appreciation to the Chief Minister by Habuild Health Tech Pvt. Ltd., in recognition of his guidance and the State’s participation in initiatives promoting yoga, health and wellness.

As part of the programme, the Chief Minister, along with other dignitaries, participated in the plantation of medicinal plants at the project site.

A video on the Yoga Tonic initiative for school students was released during the programme, followed by a video presentation of the complex showcasing the proposed Wellness and Happiness Centres, highlighting the planned facilities and key features of the complex.

A video presentation on AYUSH services was also featured, highlighting various initiatives undertaken by the Department to strengthen healthcare services and extend their reach across the State.

A health camp and a mobile village clinic were also set up at the venue, providing healthcare services to participants.

Also present at the occasion were, zilla members; panchayat members; officials from AYUSH; officials from various department and members of the public.

text:
I remember the hype around GMOs in the 1990s. People were going to be eating all these exotic fruits and vegetables. Things that never existed before 

It never happened. A generation on, and the visible variety of foods offered to consumers very few GMO products 

The reason is because there is a proportion of consumers who are highly resistant to anything even hinting at GMO tech. They won’t buy it, and they organize vociferously against it. For food companies, it just isn’t worth it. They mostly avoided the technology as a result 

GMOs do exist in the system. But they’re invisible to consumers for the most part. Where you find GMOs is in the inputs, for example seed oils and corn syrup, or as feed for livestock. 

AI games can easily end up the same way. AI is obviously very useful in terms coding, and so you’ll see AI being used invisibly in terms of the various tools that go into crafting a game. Almost no one knows the various systems used to produce games today, unless they’re in the industry themselves, so this won’t be much a change. But the games themselves will remain human crafted. It won’t take that many. Maybe 20% of people refusing to play AI games will be enough

text:
SEOUL'S BOUNCE IS BEING BOUGHT AT HOME. FOREIGN MONEY HAS SOLD 13 SESSIONS IN A ROW AND IS SELLING AGAIN:

Asia is winning back part of Thursday's chip rout, and in Seoul, where the exchange posts a running count of who is buying, the money is local. Foreign investors, net sellers there for 13 straight sessions, are selling again on Friday. In Taipei, TSMC, the chipmaker that reported a record quarter on Thursday, is sitting out its own market's rally.

The verdict at 9:30pm ET: Asia's own investors are buying back markets that fell hard, and the money that left has not come back. Until foreign investors turn buyers, this is a rebound after heavy selling, not a sign the selling is over.

Friday so far, each from Thursday's close, as of 9:20pm to 9:40pm ET:

- Nikkei 225 (Japan): 65,633, +1,207 points / +1.87%.
- KOSPI (South Korea): 5,687.86, +133.64 points / +2.41%.
- Taiex (Taiwan): 47,387.03, +417.16 points / +0.89%.
- Hang Seng (Hong Kong): 24,360.70, +297.98 points / +1.24%, seven minutes after its open.
- Shanghai Composite: 3,720.40, +12.92 points / +0.35%, seven minutes after its open.

Seoul and Taipei have each won back more than a quarter of Thursday's fall, and Tokyo more than a third (arithmetic). The timing has changed, too. On Thursday, Tokyo and Seoul set their highs for the day in the first ten minutes and slid the rest of the way. On Friday, both set their highs more than an hour in. Seoul's best level so far, 5,745.36, came after 10am local time. Both have eased off those highs since, so the first hour proved buyers showed up, not that they will stay.

Who is buying matters more than how much. By 10:30am in Seoul, foreign investors had sold a net 336 billion won of stock, about $249M (arithmetic), by the Korea Exchange's running count. Korean institutions and individuals were the net buyers. If that holds to the close, it will be the 14th straight session of foreign selling in Seoul's main market. The 13 before it, since September 23, add up to about 27.4 trillion won, roughly $20B at Friday's exchange rate (arithmetic).

The buying still reaches almost everything: 781 Seoul stocks were up and 114 down. Local money is lifting the whole market, and foreign money is selling into it.

The currency points the same way. The won is about 0.4% weaker against the dollar since Thursday afternoon in New York. The yen and the Taiwan dollar have moved less than half as much. Foreign investors who sell Korean shares and take the money home have to sell won to do it. That fits the count; it is a reading of the prices, not a reported cause.

Taipei offers the second clue: its benchmark is up, and its biggest company is not.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) at $422.25, -$7.75 / -1.80% on Thursday, and $422.83 after hours, +$0.58 / +0.14% from that close.

TSMC makes the chips other companies design, most AI processors among them. On Thursday it reported a record quarter and raised its 2026 sales growth forecast to about 44% in dollars. New York sold its US shares anyway. Taipei had its first chance at 9pm ET. In its first half hour, TSMC never moved more than half a percent from Thursday's close. The index around it rose almost 1%.

Two parts of Thursday's call give buyers a reason to wait. Gross margin, what TSMC keeps from each sales dollar after the cost of making the chips, was 66.4% in the September quarter. Its forecast for December is 65%-67%, held down by the cost of ramping up its newest 2-nanometer chips. And chief executive C.C. Wei said consumer and price-sensitive markets "are being challenged due to the impact of rising component prices," adding, "we are being prudent in our business planning going into 2027." No outlet has tied TSMC's flat start to those remarks; that is a reading of the prices, not a reported cause.

TSMC sits on none of the six Len5 watchlists: the nearest, Momentum, hunts stocks climbing to new highs, and its US shares sit 13.1% under their October 5 closing high (arithmetic).

New York's futures have not followed Asia. Each since Thursday's settlement, the exchange's official end-of-day price, as of 9:20pm ET:

- S&P 500 futures: 7,789.00, -2.00 points / -0.03%.
- Nasdaq-100 futures: 30,060.25, -83.50 points / -0.28%.
- Dow futures: 52,458.00, +28.00 points / +0.05%.
- Russell 2000 futures: 2,781.80, +0.00 points / +0.00%.

Only the contract built from the biggest US tech companies has moved more than a tenth of a percent, and it is lower. Read alongside Seoul's foreign selling, that says global money has not come back to AI chips tonight, even as Asia's local money has. Overnight moves this small can fade or flip before New York's regular session opens at 9:30am ET.

What would make this more than a rebound: foreign investors ending Seoul's session as net buyers, and TSMC trading clearly above Thursday's close in Taipei. What would show it fading: Seoul's gain shrinking through the afternoon while the foreign selling grows.

What comes next, Eastern time:

- 11:30pm: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh in conversation with IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva in Bangkok, with Tokyo, Seoul, Taipei and Hong Kong all trading.
- 1:30am: Taipei closes.
- 2:30am: Tokyo and Seoul close, and the Korea Exchange's full-day count of foreign buying and selling follows.
- 9:30am: New York's regular session opens.

The key risk: any hint from Warsh of another rate increase while Asia is still trading. Rate fears fed Thursday's selling, and Friday's local buyers have not yet faced fresh news.

Asia's rally has buyers. It does not yet have the ones who left.

text:
THE GOD PARTICLE - ARE WE LIVING IN THE ORIGINAL CREATION?

I had a thought about CERN, the Higgs boson, the Mandela effect and the structure of existence itself. 

Follow me down this rabbit hole.

The central idea is simple. 

God created the universe, also the laws governing matter and energy. 

Those laws contain the mechanisms of creation itself.

Particles collide. 
Energy transforms. 
New structures emerge.

That is the foundation of reality.

Now consider CERN. 

Humanity built a machine capable of accelerating particles to extraordinary energies and smashing them together under conditions resembling those of the early universe. 

Scientists use these collisions to study the fundamental particles and forces that shape existence.

The Higgs boson was famously nicknamed the “God particle.”

That name raises an intriguing question. 

What if the interactions CERN studies do more than reveal the building blocks of reality?

What if, under certain conditions, they can generate entirely new configurations of reality?

Not another universe somewhere beyond our reach, but a new simulation emerging within an existing one.

In this theory, creation is recursive. 

A universe could arise from processes occurring inside another universe, just as that universe may have emerged from an earlier reality. 

Creation would not be a single event in the distant past, but an ongoing process.. reality generating reality through the laws established at the beginning of existence.

This possibility also offers a speculative way to think about the Mandela effect. 

Millions of people report conflicting memories of names, events, images and histories. 

The conventional explanation is that human memory is unreliable.

But what if these inconsistencies reflect something deeper?

What if different realities have emerged, intersected or inherited fragments of histories that were once separate? 

The version of history we experience might not be the original timeline, but the history carried forward by our current reality.

That would explain why conflicting memories can feel so certain. 

They may not belong to one shared past. 

They may be remnants of different versions of reality.

CERN did not invent particle collisions. 

The universe has been producing them since its earliest moments. 

But what if humanity has begun reproducing, on a limited scale, the same kinds of interactions through which reality itself was formed?

If a new configuration of reality could emerge within an existing one, the consequences would be impossible to predict. 

Would the two realities remain separate? 

Would their histories overlap?

Could information, memory or physical laws carry across the boundary?

This is where the theory becomes most unsettling. 

Our universe may not be the original creation at all. 

It could be the result of an interaction within another reality, which itself emerged from another, continuing backward without a final identifiable beginning.

There would be no single timeline containing the whole truth. 

There would only be layers of existence, each producing the conditions for the next.

The irony is that humanity named the Higgs boson the “God particle” while using it to investigate the fundamental structure of creation. 

Perhaps we are not merely studying how the universe works. 

But we are learning how the universe can be generated.

God wrote the laws of existence. 

Humanity learned to manipulate the particles governed by them.

So the question is not whether CERN created a new universe.

We have no evidence that it did.

The deeper question is whether the laws of physics contain a repeatable pathway to creation, and whether humanity has begun to understand it.

Are we living in the original creation, or inside one of countless realities born from the same divine laws?

That's my simulation theory. 

And it's one hell of a rabbit hole. 💯🔥🤍

Washington state school district agrees to apologize, pay $275,000 to Bible ed group https://t.co/wFq07Kp7kt 
Washington state school district agrees to apologize, pay $275,000 to Bible ed group
“This is a tremendous victory not only for our clients but for all religious release time programs,” an attorney for the Christian group said.
Jessica Russak-Hoffman
RepublishCopyLink copiedEmail
Print

📷An open bible on a desk. Credit: RDNE Stock project/Pexels.
(Oct. 15, 2026 / JNS)
Everett Public Schools, a Washington state public school district with about 20,700 students in 27 schools, agreed to pay $275,000 in attorney’s fees and to apologize to families to settle a lawsuit over its treatment of LifeWise Academy, which offers off-campus Bible instruction during school hours.
Attorneys for the academy accused the district of imposing restrictions other programs didn’t face, including requiring weekly parental permission and rules requiring students to keep LifeWise materials in sealed envelopes in their backpacks.
The First Liberty Institute, which represents LifeWise, said on Tuesday that the settlement requires the district school board to undergo religious liberty training and includes revisions to district policies on religious activities.
“Religious discrimination has no place in public schools,” stated Stephanie Taub, senior counsel at the institute. “This is a tremendous victory not only for our clients but for all religious release time programs.”
Attorneys cited school board member Charles Adkins, who allegedly said at a board meeting that he wanted “to make it very, extremely, abundantly clear, that yes, I do in fact hold animus toward LifeWise Academy.”

The settlement requires the district to post an apology on its website and keep it posted for six months.

According to First Liberty, the district will apologize for the statement at the school board meeting.

It will say, in part, that “the district values the rights of all families to raise their children according to their own religious beliefs” and that “we further apologize to any students or families that were made to feel by these comments that your religious beliefs are unworthy of respect,” according to the institute.

The district states on its website that it neither endorses nor opposes religious programs. Its published guidelines limit release for religious instruction to lunch or recess, require parental authorization and leave transportation arrangements to families.

-----------------------------
After I had just completed my first hospital round earlier this morning, while driving to the next healthcare facility, I had this thought at a traffic light stop that just seemed to be quite strong about what we could do to see a healthier church in terms of unity in the years to come. 

First of all, I thank God for the passage of Ephesians 4:11-16 that Paul wrote showing that this unity is possible. Without the vision of the finished product, attempts to try seem to be in vain. We know what the current church is. We know the bickering. We have seen the manipulations. We understand the intrigues. Underhanded dealings. Dirty money and corruption everywhere. Filthy speech of "discernment ministries" attacking Charismatic pastors. Church politics. 

It never ends. 

So, is there hope ?

Last night I offered some solutions. Like Calvinists being more knowledgeable about Pentecostal teachings and Charismatics being more knowledgeable about Calvinism. However, this might be too simplistic, considering some of the Pentecostal/Charismatic vs Pentecostal/Charismatic attacks you see in Nigeria. There are not just inter-denominational fights, there are also intra-tribe factions. You can smell the works of the flesh everywhere. 

I could add 4 other practical things beyond those I shared last night.

𝟏. 𝐀𝐢𝐦 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐡𝐞𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐮𝐧𝐢𝐭𝐲

The sense of understanding the problem and seeing other people's weaknesses can create a false sense of superiority, as though we are better. This can lead to self-righteousness [Luke 18: 9-14]. 

"𝘐 𝘢𝘮 𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘭𝘪𝘬𝘦 𝘑𝘶𝘴𝘵𝘪𝘯 𝘗𝘦𝘵𝘦𝘳𝘴."

"𝘐 𝘢𝘮 𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘭𝘪𝘬𝘦 𝘚𝘱𝘪𝘳𝘪𝘤𝘰𝘤𝘰."

First of all, I would not be able to vouch for Justin Peter's salvation, so I am not sure if being better than him would have any worth. We should not find our value in comparing ourselves to the worst humans in the world. 

Paul sees a perfect church in unity emerging [Ephesians 4:13]. And in that church our distinction or the difference we make or the flavor we bring to mix or the value we add to the church is not about try to be better than those who are in error, rather seeking to glorify God in whatever we do [Isaiah 42:8; 1 Corinthians 10:31]. 

Companies exist to solve problems-- which means they need those problems to prove their "raison d'Être"

Spiritual people in the church do not need to witness the current dysfunction in order to prove their usefulness in healing the fractured tribes within Christendom. 

We should aim for total restoration and unity where correction of error will no longer be necessary. 

𝟐. 𝐃𝐲𝐬𝐟𝐮𝐧𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐞𝐩𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐞𝐮𝐫𝐬

The aim of the first category should not necessarily presuppose the immediate disappearance of "dysfunction entrepreneurs."  Just like those who are more enlightened, more matured, and have a broader acceptance of various belief systems and practices within Christendom could be at risk of pride in their advanced understanding of Scriptures, those who run "discernment ministries" are at risk of always looking for dirt, fault-finding efforts [Jude 1:16]-- and in short they will never see Ephesians 4:13 and John 17:21 as realistic or practical this side of heaven. They see those Scriptures as mere suggestions, not God's intent for the Body of Christ. Dysfunction must exist because this is their work. It is why they raise money. It is what they get paid to do. It is why they exist. No dysfunction, no job. 

Now, the third category below is added because of the Jude 1:3 scenario of "contending for the faith." We should never try to argue that there are no legitimate fraudulent preachers within the Charismatic movement, just as there are plenty of shady, controlling, rigid, adulterous, hateful-murderous pastors within the Calvinist community. The leaven is in both camps. The effort to remove it cannot be dismissed, if done properly [1 Corinthians 5:6; Luke 12:1]. 

𝟑. 𝐂𝐨𝐫𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐣𝐮𝐝𝐠𝐞 𝐥𝐞𝐠𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐫𝐞𝐛𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧

So, if we pray for "dysfunction entrepreneurs" to go away [Matthew 15:13]- then those who are truly left doing sincere Jude 1:3 contending should be aiming for a proper ending of the need to address dysfunction.

A. Correction that leads to repentance [2 Timothy 2:24-25]. Hopefully within 6 months of providing solid evidence of the need to repent. 

B. Prayer and expectation for judgment [1 Peter 4:17]- where that repentance has been resistance and there is open rebellion challenging the Word of God. 

4. 𝐏𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐥𝐲 𝐞𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐝𝐞𝐜𝐞𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐝 𝐨𝐧 𝐝𝐨𝐜𝐭𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐬

90% of the sheep have no idea why they get involved in the fights they are in [Acts 19:32]. If everyone in your church is attacking pastor XYZ and you do not seem to be doing it, disloyalty may be levelled against you as an accusation. This is especially so in Africa apparently. Loyalty to one apostle must be proven by willing to attack another pastor or evangelist. If you do not participate in the attack, you may not get promoted or invited to speak. Defending your tribe by destroying the reputation of the other tribe is a form of survivalism. 

Many of the ignorant sheep have been recruited to fight and die in battles that their recruiters themselves are ashamed to be a part of. They don't know why they are fighting. They don't know why they are dying. All this time they are failing to discern the Lord's Body beyond their small circle [1 Corinthians 11:25-34]. 

Sincere efforts can be made to teach them elevated doctrines of the Word that bring them outside of their bondage into the glorious liberty of the sons of God!

text:
You are wrong. If you understood scripture, and had read the Bible, you would not have asked that question. Your Prophet obviously did not understand, or did not read, scripture.

Here is a brief summary of what Jesus, and the Bible, says about the food we eat:

Jesus declared all foods clean.
 “Do you not see that whatever goes into a person from outside cannot defile him…?” (Mark 7:18). Mark adds that Jesus thereby “declared all foods clean” (Mark 7:19).

•  Nothing is unclean in itself.
 Paul writes, “I know and am persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself” (Romans 14:14). He adds that “everything is indeed clean” (Romans 14:20).

•  All creatures are good when received with thanksgiving.
 “For every creature of God is good, and nothing is to be refused if it is received with thanksgiving, for it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer” (1 Timothy 4:4–5).

•  Do not let anyone judge you over food.
 “Therefore let no one pass judgment on you in questions of food and drink… These are a shadow of the things to come, but the substance belongs to Christ” (Colossians 2:16–17).

Remaining practical limits

•  Acts 15 (the Jerusalem Council) asked Gentile believers to abstain from food offered to idols, blood, and meat from strangled animals (Acts 15:20, 29). These were primarily to avoid idolatry and unnecessary offense to Jewish believers.

•  1 Corinthians 8 and 10 address food sacrificed to idols. Believers have liberty (“Everything is permissible”), but they should not exercise it in a way that causes another person to stumble or that participates in idol worship (1 Cor. 8:4–13; 10:23–31). Eat what is sold in the meat market without raising questions of conscience (1 Cor. 10:25–26).

The New Testament removes the clean/unclean distinctions of the Old Testament food laws. Food is a matter of liberty, to be received gratefully. The main ongoing concerns are (1) avoiding idolatry and (2) not using liberty in a way that harms a weaker believer’s conscience.
